title: Inter Miami’s German Berterame conscious in hospital after head collision, says coach
content:
Inter Miami forward German Berterame is conscious and recovering in hospital after suffering a head collision in Saturday’s MLS game against Montreal, his coach Guillermo Hoyos has said.

In the 70th minute at Saputo Stadium, Berterame was involved in an aerial collision with Montreal defender Efrain Morales and landed awkwardly on the pitch, appearing to lose consciousness. Montreal’s Brayan Vera immediately called for medical assistance as several players of both teams attended to the 27-year-old.

After several minutes of receiving medical attention, Berterame — who did not appear to have regained consciouscness — was taken off the pitch on a stretcher and transferred into an ambulance.

“He’s recovering right now, he’s fine, conscious,” Hoyos told reporters after the game.

“His family is aware of everything. They’re calm. The most important thing is that he’s OK, and right now he is OK.

“We were alarmed at first because the blow was very strong. On the play, it’s obvious there was an elbow, which is why a penalty was awarded, he fell like dead weight.

“I think he might have already been unconscious given the severity of the impact. He took that elbow and hit the ground hard. It was a moment of great desperation and deep sadness, because it went beyond football, and all that. It’s about human life, that’s what matters most. So, we just hope everything turns out well.”

Inter Miami were awarded a penalty owing to the incident, which Luis Suarez converted to score the only goal of the game for his side’s victory. The Uruguayan striker held up Berterame’s Inter Miami shirt in honour of his team-mate after scoring.

Mexico international Berterame has scored seven MLS goals for Inter Miami since joining from Monterrey in January.

Saturday’s victory was Inter Miami’s sixth in a row and consolidated its position in second in the Eastern Conference, two points behind leaders Nashville. Montreal, without an MLS win in six attempts, stay 13th.
